type: which grouping is the better prior for an unseen drug
why_not_the_previous_gate: R144 asked for a shrunk marginal baseline, but an unseen drug has n = 0 so any shrinkage collapses to the grand mean; the only source of information is a grouping, so the meaningful competitor is a different grouping
answer: use pathway, not target; adding target on top is not worth the dimensions

what_this_rules_out.point: target is the finer partition and performs worse, so a granularity explanation is excluded, independently supporting C108

what_this_settles.earlier: R106 compared pathway against target and found only one of three pools significant
what_this_settles.why: it used the sparse boolean criterion which cannot resolve this in that pool (R122, R131)

degeneracy_note: no arm here was degenerate; all five have non-zero dispersion and the random grouping sits at zero
limits: Only this resource and only ridge.
Target has 98 levels against pathway's 38; this round uses that as an argument rather than treating it as a defect.
Retrospective; no mechanism, clinical or drug-choice claim.
next_gate: test whether pathway remains the best substitute under cross-tissue transfer
